objectives: Recognise -ap and -at CVC patterns containing the newly taught p.
Compare p-containing words by their changing phoneme.
Use word-family patterns as support while continuing full grapheme decoding.
concepts: Word families make repeated spelling patterns visible.
A shared ending does not make words identical.
Pattern recognition supports but never replaces decoding.

definitions.definition: A group of words sharing a common sound and spelling ending.
Reading material built mainly from patterns and correspondences already taught.

workedExamples: map → tap changes the initial phoneme
pat → mat changes the initial phoneme
commonMistakes: Guessing a family member without checking its first sound.
Ignoring the final phoneme when comparing words.

application: Build a new word by changing one known phoneme.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why a word-family pattern cannot replace grapheme-by-grapheme decoding.
mixedReview: Classify, decode, compare and reread p-containing words.

formulaOrFactBank: Word family = shared ending pattern + different initial phoneme(s)
mistakeBasedRevision: If map is confused with mat, isolate and rehearse the final /p/ versus /t/.
weakTopicRevision: Read short mixed -ap/-at sets and repeat only words with decoding errors.

activities.name: One-sound change
steps: Change the first sound to make tap.

activities.name: Controlled reread
steps: Read a small p-word family set.

outcomes: Learner classifies at least 8 of 10 familiar p-containing CVC words into taught families.
Learner identifies the changing phoneme in related CVC words.
Learner rereads a small controlled p-word set accurately.
